When a company acquires another business for more than the fair value of its net identifiable assets, the excess is recorded as goodwill. Under GAAP, goodwill is not amortised but it is tested for impairment at least once a year, and the carrying amount of a reporting unit exceeds its fair value, the company has to write down the difference. This is different from intangible assets with a finite life, like patents and customer lists, which are amortised over their useful lives. And the auditors will want to see the assumptions behind the discounted cash flow model, especially the discount rate and the terminal road rate.
